value.rationale: A motivated noncontracting gap for implicit state-dependent feedback is resolved by a structural global theorem: only a one-sided downward slope bound is needed for linear response, permitting arbitrarily steep upward events. An exact periodic forced example separates well-posed and invisible implicit feedback from a nonconverging finite nesting procedure. This sharp conceptual distinction is useful for delay modelling and is neither merely a normalization check nor a routine isolated parameter example.
